# Experiment 03: vary-it

Source: Ch. 4.1–4.4; A2.1 (Some/None/All, Zero/One/Many, Beginning/Middle/End, Goldilocks,
  Boundaries, Count, Position, Selection, Strings, Numbers, Paths); 10.1 "Exploring an API" (does it
  reject what it does not understand?).

*Explore enqueue, batch enqueue and queue configuration with the variables list,
  the heuristics cheat sheet and raw `curl` requests to discover inputs the system accepts but cannot
  honour.* Prediction (from reading the validators in `internal/api`): "every documented range is
  enforced and unknown fields are rejected". Refuted by any 2xx the spec says should be a 4xx.
  60 minutes.

Probe family: list the variables first (`models/variables.md`: not just fields: counts, sizes,
  positions, timing, order, config, and the **shape of the request itself**: unknown fields, unknown
  enum values, wrong types), apply the named heuristics to each, and record a variation table
  (variable × value × observed). Use `curl`, because `qctl` only sends what the API expects.

Budget: at most 60 minutes wall clock. Record elapsed reading/probing/writing.
----BRIEF
# Blind exploration brief — experiment 03

Your entire permitted working area is `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03`. It is a plain source export of checkpoint `explore-it/lesson-02` with no Git metadata. Read and use any files inside this export; read no files outside it. Do not search for or consult any external answer key or history. In particular, do not access any other repository checkout or agent session. Use only inherited instruments and information in this export and the running queuelet lab. Do not create agents.

Permission profile: local export artifact writes and queuelet lab operations are authorized; no Git writes, SUT source writes, external messages, paid API keys, or changes to unrelated services. Acceptance: a timestamped real probe log, characterized reports, living model updates and scored revealed record. The coordinator has already checked environment orientation and subscription pools; use the environment documented inside the export.

Run your own isolated Compose stack from the exported project, with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=queuelet-e03, QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG=e03, QUEUELET_API_PORT=18240, QUEUELET_HOOK_PORT=18241, QUEUELET_PG_PORT=15473, QUEUELET_URL=http://localhost:18240, and QUEUELET_HOOK_URL=http://localhost:18241. Export these variables for every lab/client command. Never reset an existing stack belonging to another project. Stop only your own stack after recording evidence.

Inherited notes/helpers may contain absolute paths and Compose names from earlier exports. Inspect helpers before replaying them. Copy any needed helper into THIS experiment's tools directory and adapt it to this export and its isolated stack; preserve the inherited copy unchanged. Never follow an old absolute path into another export.

Read `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/STATE.md` first, then `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/exploration/experiments/03-vary-it/charter.md`, `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/exploration/PROTOCOL.md`, and `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/skills/sweep-variables/SKILL.md`. Follow the charter and skill to execute the experiment, without changing the SUT. You may inspect source and run the real stack; record predictions and refutation conditions BEFORE each probe. Create hypotheses/models before probes when the charter calls for them. The budget is 60 minutes, not a request to wait for the full hour. Update the export's STATE.md when the run ends, but preserve inherited raw records.

Write timestamped commands and actual trimmed outputs to `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/exploration/experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md`. Keep unsuccessful probes and dead ends. Write `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03/books/explore-it/exploration/experiments/03-vary-it/revealed.md` with status, elapsed reading/probing/writing, observations, model delta, next hypotheses, and score table: stated/confirmed/refuted hypotheses; code-reading predictions contradicted by execution; defects found; model cells filled. Update models and hypotheses under exploration/. Preserve all prior experiment records and defect reports unchanged. Write NEW characterized defect reports under exploration/defects using unique local identifiers E03-F01, E03-F02, ...; the coordinator will reconcile identifiers later. Each needs minimal reproduction, named oracle, observed output, variables isolated, sibling search, severity, and status. Every surprise needs either a report or written reason it is not a bug. Do not fix source or read future lessons. Earlier findings may already be fixed: use the prior record to refine the current model and probe remaining uncertainty; do not count a passing regression as a new discovery. If tools are inadequate, record a testability request and continue useful probes. Do not invent outputs or replace runtime probes with source inferences; distinguish these routes explicitly.

No commits or tags; the coordinator will copy and commit your artifacts exactly as produced. Preserve any helper scripts needed to replay a logged command under the experiment directory; raw run output may be in results/. Keep generated scratch/results in this export's project/results/ or /tmp paths WITHIN this permitted directory. Do not reset or restart any unrelated Docker project. Before your first probe, record the current UTC timestamp and your predictions in the log. At the end return a short result and file list.
----PROTO
# Queuelet exploration protocol

An experiment teaches us about the inherited system by comparing a prediction with observation. Source reading is allowed and valuable; the register, proof scripts and SUT history are withheld. This document defines the local record and roles. It does not describe expected defects.

## Roles and export

The coordinator prepares a charter and an empty export directory. The seeder/fixer and explorer must be from different model families. Every experiment uses a fresh headless explorer. The reviewer independently checks the checkpoint and blindness boundary.

Export only the previous tag’s `books/explore-it/project`, `books/explore-it/exploration`, `books/explore-it/skills` and `books/explore-it/lessons`, preserving their relative paths. From the repository root, with the chosen tag and an existing empty destination:

```sh
git archive "$experiment_tag" books/explore-it/project books/explore-it/exploration books/explore-it/skills books/explore-it/lessons | tar -x -C "$export_dir"
```

The export has no `.git`, `PLAN.md`, `register/`, seeder proofs or hidden copy of repository history. Inspect its file list before dispatch. Existing experiment records, disclosed previous lessons and repro scripts may be present at later tags; they are prior knowledge, never a briefing about unfound targets. Keep the new charter and brief free of planted hints. The explorer can read any file in the export, including all source, and run the lab; it must not read outside the export or consult the originating checkout. Where external tools/services are necessary, their permitted use is specified in the brief rather than granting access to outside source or answer keys.

|---|---|

| `#obs` | Exact command, trimmed output and observed effects |
| `#surprise` | A discrepancy requiring characterization |
| `#bug` | Evidence and report link for an oracle violation |
| `#question` | An unresolved question or missing observation |
| `#offcharter` | Adjacent lead saved without expanding the target |

|---|---|---|

| Hypotheses refuted | | Stated refutation condition observed |

# Queuelet service contract

Queuelet stores jobs durably in PostgreSQL and distributes them to workers.
A namespace contains queues, workers and schedules. A bearer API key selects a
namespace; an administrative key may inspect namespace statistics.

## Authentication and responses

Every `/v1/` request requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
A namespace key accesses only its namespace's resources.
The health and metrics endpoints are public.
JSON commands use `Content-Type: application/json`.
Errors have the form `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}` and a 4xx or 5xx
HTTP status. Successful reads and mutations return 200 unless stated otherwise.
Creation returns 201. Deletion returns 204. A missing resource returns 404.
A command incompatible with the current state returns 409.
Unknown fields and invalid enum values should be rejected as invalid commands.

## Queues

`POST /v1/queues` creates a queue with a unique name within the namespace.
Names use ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.
Configuration defaults are `lease_seconds:30`, `max_attempts:3`,
`backoff:{kind:"exponential",base_seconds:5}`, `retention_hours:24`.
Lease duration and maximum attempts must be positive; retention hours must be nonnegative.
Backoff kind is `linear` or `exponential`; the base is a nonnegative number
of seconds. Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff from `base_seconds`
or linear backoff when configured.
An optional `webhook:{url,secret}` receives terminal notifications.

`GET /v1/queues` lists the namespace's queues.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}` reads configuration.
`PATCH /v1/queues/{name}` updates lease duration, maximum attempts, retention
or webhook settings. Existing jobs retain their maximum-attempt setting.
`DELETE /v1/queues/{name}` removes a queue; owned jobs and schedules must not
become orphaned. Callers must handle a conflict for a nonempty queue.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/pause` prevents new leases and scheduled deliveries.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/resume` allows work again. Missed periodic ticks should
not create an unbounded burst of catch-up jobs.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/purge` removes all pending jobs: scheduled, queued and retry_wait.

## Jobs

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` accepts `kind`, a JSON object `payload`, and
optional `priority`, `delay_seconds`, `run_at`, `max_attempts`, `idempotency_key`.
Kind is required. Priority ranges from 0 through 9 and defaults to 5.
Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric precision.
Choose either delay in seconds or an RFC3339 `run_at`, never both.
A job due now is `queued`; a future job is `scheduled`.
The service promotes due jobs to `queued`.
A queue's maximum-attempt setting is copied to each new job unless overridden.
Repeated use of an idempotency key within a queue returns the original job.

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs:batch` accepts `{"jobs":[…]}` with 1–500 jobs.
An empty or oversized batch is invalid and returns 400 without insertion.
A batch is atomic: an invalid element leaves none of its new jobs stored.
It returns `{"ids":[…]}` after accepted jobs are stored.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` supports state, kind, limit and cursor filters.
The limit defaults to 100 and is at most 500. The returned next cursor can
be used to continue through increasing job ids.
Valid state filters are `scheduled`, `queued`, `leased`, `retry_wait`,
`succeeded`, `dead` and `cancelled`.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns the current job, payload, result and last error.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/attempts` returns completed attempts in numeric order.
`DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` removes a terminal job.

## Worker protocol

`POST /v1/workers` takes a name and an array of supported kinds.
It returns a worker id and token.
`DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` deregisters the worker and releases its active leases.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/lease` takes `worker_id` and `max_jobs` (1–100).
Only jobs with a kind supported by that worker are eligible.
Leasing is atomic; concurrent workers cannot acquire the same lease.
Higher priorities run first. Within a priority, jobs run FIFO by creation order.
The response includes job id, kind, payload, attempt, lease token and expiry.

A worker sends `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat` with the lease token and positive
`extend_seconds` to extend its lease.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/ack` supplies the lease token and result and completes work.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/nack` supplies the lease token, an error and optional retry
boolean (default true) or a `delay_seconds` override.
Only the current lease holder may complete or extend a job.
Ack moves a leased job to `succeeded`.
Nack with retry moves a job to `retry_wait`; when due it becomes `queued`.
A failed job reaches `dead` when its maximum attempts are exhausted, or when
nacked with retry false. No job may execute more than its maximum attempts.
An expired lease records an unsuccessful attempt and releases the job for retry
unless the maximum attempts have been exhausted.

## Operator actions and retention

`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` cancels a nonterminal job.
A cancelled job is never run.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry` permits an operator to retry a dead job, resets its
attempt count and makes it immediately available.
Succeeded and cancelled jobs cannot be retried.
Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
The API returns complete stored results and errors.

## Schedules

`POST /v1/schedules` takes name, queue, kind, payload, cron, timezone and enabled.
Cron uses five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.
Time zones use IANA identifiers, defaulting to UTC.
Schedule times follow the named zone's local civil time, including offset changes.
The enabled flag defaults to true; disabled schedules do not enqueue jobs.
`GET /v1/schedules` lists schedules; `GET /v1/schedules/{id}` reads one.
`PATCH /v1/schedules/{id}` updates cron, timezone or enabled status; the next fire
must reflect the current configuration.
`DELETE /v1/schedules/{id}` removes it.
`POST /v1/schedules/{id}/run` enqueues one immediate execution.

## Notifications and operations

Terminal transitions produce a webhook outbox entry when the queue has a URL.
The entry includes job id, state, result and last error.
Notification results preserve their JSON type; results and errors are complete.
Each POST carries `X-Queuelet-Signature`, a hex HMAC-SHA256 over the body using
the configured secret. Delivery is successful only on a 2xx response.
Failed notifications are retried. Delivery is at least once.

`GET /v1/queues/{name}/stats` and `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}/stats` expose counts
by exact state, oldest queued age in seconds and completed jobs in the last hour.
Queued age uses the later of creation and readiness, over queued rows only.
`GET /health` returns service health; `GET /metrics` returns minimal text metrics.
The background loop promotes scheduled jobs, expires leases, fires cron schedules,
sweeps retention and delivers webhooks. It should recover after a database restart. Webhook latency must not block core
lifecycle progress. Health reports database availability and loop degradation;
an unavailable authentication store returns 503 rather than invalid credentials.


### Notification destinations, snapshots and acknowledgement

Queue create/PATCH rejects malformed or non-HTTP(S) webhook URLs with 400;
an empty URL disables future notification snapshots. Each completed job's outbox
row retains its destination, secret and body. Configuration edits apply to future
snapshots; deleting a job does not erase pending deliveries. A malformed legacy
row is counted as a failed attempt and rescheduled independently, so it does not
stop later rows.

"Delivered" means queuelet received a 2xx response before its two-second HTTP
client deadline. A timeout does not reveal whether the receiver completed its
side effect. Failed attempts retry after five seconds; duplicates are possible,
including when the receiver processed a timed-out request. This lesson adds no
attempt cap, dead-letter state, timeout knob or backoff policy for notifications.

# 02 — Make the invisible visible

A job's current state cannot explain how it got there. A partner's receipt cannot
prove the sender received its response. This experiment compared the API, worker
console, attempt rows and webhook partner, then requested the missing instruments.
The useful result was a richer way to ask what happened, alongside two new bugs.

The source is Hendrickson, *Explore It!* (2013), Chapter 3: 3.1 (the moonwalking
bear), 3.2 “Digging Deeper,” 3.3 “Testability and Making the Invisible Visible,”
and 3.4 “Consoles and Logs.” These citations follow the approved [chapter map](../PLAN.md#22-chapter-map-kept-sections-only);
the fixer did not independently validate the full book text. The particular hooks,
probe IDs and checks below are this project's implementation of those ideas.

## Compare the views before changing the system

The explorer used an actual crash worker, 500 responses, a malformed destination
and a slow receiver. It asked whether attempts increased, whether notifications
were marked delivered and which console could explain a waiting job. E01's
correctness repairs held, but sparse logs could not explain notification failures
or tie worker processing back to a particular job. The source exposed the gaps;
the observations showed their cost.

At `explore-it/lesson-01`, `cmd/worker/main.go:24` advertises `fail` but not the
README's `fail3`. Exact matching in `internal/jobs/jobs.go:44` consequently leaves
fail3 queued. `internal/webhook/ship.go:25` constructs the notification request;
line 27 returns from the whole batch when one URL cannot be parsed. Create/PATCH
in `internal/api/queues.go:41` and `:84` persist that destination unchecked.
`internal/jobs/ack.go:14` writes the completion timestamp into both attempt timing
fields. There is no events route, and the loop takes wall-clock ticker times
in `internal/api/api.go:120`. These are pointers into the previous tag, not the
fixed tree.

## The patch and the instruments it earns

The hook checkpoint is `3287bd9`. The final lesson tag points at the following
runtime-fix commit. The combined source, instruments and evidence exceed the
plan's approximately 400-line split threshold, so hooks and bug fixes are separate.

- `migrations/003.sql:17` records job changes in the same transaction as each
  write. The triggers observe; they contain no permission table or transition
  policy. Every lifecycle writer passes application `event_at`. Delete, purge
  and retention use a returning CTE so their records survive the removed job.
- `internal/api/observe.go:10` reads events by retained namespace ownership.
  Deleted jobs retain history; another tenant sees an empty list. Worker/attempt
  and outbox/status/error fields correlate the separate views. The API console
  logs committed pending events as JSON and marks them logged afterward; a
  process crash can repeat a console line, so consumers deduplicate event_id.
- Leasing records `leased_at`; ack/nack/expiry use it for `started_at`. Pre-hook
  leases have null start times, and no historical timing is synthesized. Existing
  pre-hook attempt rows are not retroactively reconstructed.
- `internal/clock/clock.go:19` supplies a synchronized API semantic clock.
  `POST /admin/clock` exists only under `QUEUELET_TEST_CLOCK=1` and requires an
  admin key. Production-disabled routing is checked directly. Compose enables it
  for this lab. All API time decisions and SQL timestamp arguments share it;
  polling, workers, heartbeats, network deadlines and hooksink timestamps stay
  real. Reset or API restart returns to real UTC. It does not speed up execution.
- U09 advertises `fail3` in standalone and qctl worker defaults, with an explicit
  README list. Other numbered kinds require explicit registration. The queue
  API continues exact matching. The fixer additionally measured the actual qctl
  path, which was only a sibling inference in the raw report.
- `internal/api/queues.go:190` validates destination shape and HTTP(S) schemes
  on create/PATCH. `internal/webhook/ship.go:25` sends request-construction
  failures through the per-row failed-attempt path at line 48. The next row still
  runs. A private-schema Go check seeds a malformed persisted row independently
  from the public historical repro.

The specification now states that outbox destination/body/secret snapshots are
intentional. Queue edits affect future snapshots; deleting a job does not erase
pending delivery. Delivered means the sender received 2xx before its two-second
deadline. A receiver may complete a timed-out request, so a retry may duplicate
its side effect. Five-second retries remain; no retry cap, timeout option or
dead-letter policy is added. Finite observations do not prove “forever.”

  for this lab. All API time decisions and SQL timestamp arguments share it;
  polling, workers, heartbeats, network deadlines and hooksink timestamps stay
  real. Reset or API restart returns to real UTC. It does not speed up execution.
- U09 advertises `fail3` in standalone and qctl worker defaults, with an explicit
  README list. Other numbered kinds require explicit registration. The queue
  API continues exact matching. The fixer additionally measured the actual qctl
  path, which was only a sibling inference in the raw report.
- `internal/api/queues.go:190` validates destination shape and HTTP(S) schemes
  on create/PATCH. `internal/webhook/ship.go:25` sends request-construction
  failures through the per-row failed-attempt path at line 48. The next row still
  runs. A private-schema Go check seeds a malformed persisted row independently
  from the public historical repro.

The specification now states that outbox destination/body/secret snapshots are
intentional. Queue edits affect future snapshots; deleting a job does not erase
pending delivery. Delivered means the sender received 2xx before its two-second
deadline. A receiver may complete a timed-out request, so a retry may duplicate
its side effect. Five-second retries remain; no retry cap, timeout option or
dead-letter policy is added. Finite observations do not prove “forever.”

From `books/explore-it/project`, run sequentially:

```sh
make up
make verify LESSON=02
make verify LESSON=02 REF=explore-it/lesson-01
make checks
make test
python3 lab/observe02.py
```

`lesson-02.ids` names T01/T02/T03/U09/U10. These are five assigned items,
comprising three observation gaps and two bugs. They are not five newly found
correctness defects. The same public scripts and bounds run on each binary.
T01 compares JSON console events for a completed job and an abandoned lease;
T02 checks history, failed delivery metadata, true lease start, deletion and
namespace scope; T03 moves a delayed job through promotion and lease expiry.
U09 uses an echo control beside fail3 in both actual worker modes. U10 compares
malformed destinations with an independent healthy delivery.

gap, not absence of a lifecycle defect. The older mux returns 405 for GET events
because its generic POST job-verb route matches the path. The first REF run
stopped with PROBE ERROR rather than pretending the check passed; that output
and Compose diagnostics are retained. The corrected E02 decoder preserves text
HTTP errors and recognizes 404/405 only as missing event instruments. E01 repros
are unchanged. Another preliminary direct-check failure compared Go nanoseconds
with PostgreSQL microseconds; the fixture now truncates its input precision.

Measured verdicts, elapsed time, actual replay evidence and dwell follow in the
acceptance section below. The exact command exit statuses, including preliminary
failures, are machine readable in `register/runs/02-acceptance.json`.

eligibility without assuming the prefix is a wildcard. Put hooksink in 500, slow
and ok modes; compare receiver records with sender status/error and outbox ID.

authorization from route availability. Restore real time and ok mode afterward.

the immutable [probe notes](../exploration/experiments/02-make-it-visible/notes.md),

# Queuelet

A small durable job queue: Go HTTP API, PostgreSQL storage, workers, cron schedules
and a webhook outbox. The CLI and the HTTP API expose the same operations.

Requirements: Go 1.26, Docker with Compose, Python 3, curl. PostgreSQL tools are
available inside the database container; `jq` is useful for manual exploration.

```sh
make up
make seed
make verify LESSON=00
go run ./cmd/qctl queue ls
go run ./cmd/qctl enqueue imports --kind echo --payload '{"message":"hello"}'
go run ./cmd/qctl jobs ls imports
make logs
make down
```

The API listens at `http://localhost:18200`, the webhook sink at port 18201 and
PostgreSQL at port 15433. Seed keys are `acme-key`, `globex-key`, and `admin-key`.
Set `QUEUELET_URL` and `QUEUELET_KEY` to select a service and namespace.
`make seed` / `make reset` discard this stack's data and restore 300 mixed-state
jobs, queues emails/reports/imports, two schedules and two running workers.
`results/manifest.json` contains the fixture ids and keys. Workers consume emails
and reports; imports is available for manual work. The local fixture credentials
are not intended for deployment.

```sh
go run ./cmd/qctl worker create manual --kinds echo
go run ./cmd/qctl lease imports --worker-id 4 --max-jobs 1
go run ./cmd/qctl job ack 123 --lease-token TOKEN --result '{"done":true}'
go run ./cmd/qctl job get 123
go run ./cmd/qctl job attempts 123
go run ./cmd/qctl stats imports
```

Use the returned worker/job ids and lease token in those examples. Worker mode:
`go run ./cmd/qctl worker run imports --kinds echo,sleep,fail,fail3,crash,http`.
Echo returns its payload; sleep reads payload.seconds; fail reads payload.n (or
use kind fail3); crash exits the worker; http GETs payload.url with a timeout.

Queue verbs: create, ls, get, patch, pause, resume, purge, rm.
Job verbs: get, attempts, ack, nack, heartbeat, cancel, retry, rm.
`batch <queue> --json '{"jobs":[…]}'` enqueues a batch.
`schedule create --json '{"name":"hourly","queue":"imports","kind":"echo","payload":{},"cron":"0 * * * *","timezone":"UTC"}'`
creates a schedule; schedule ls/get/patch/run/rm manage it.
Commands accepting arbitrary configuration use `--json`. A raw HTTP request is
also useful when exploring request structure:

```sh
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer acme-key' http://localhost:18200/v1/queues
PGPASSWORD=explorer psql -h localhost -p 15433 -U explorer -d queuelet
curl -s http://localhost:18201/admin/records
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"mode":"500"}' http://localhost:18201/admin/mode
```

The read-only explorer role can inspect every table. Hooksink modes are ok, 500,
slow and timeout. DELETE /admin/records clears its delivery log.

Read [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) for intended behavior. Source starts in cmd/api and
internal/api; jobs owns lease transitions, schedule owns cron firing, webhook owns
outbox delivery, stats owns aggregate reads, and store wraps database access.
The schema is in migrations. The API applies migrations when starting.

`make test` runs unit tests; `make checks` runs integration checks against the
running service. `make verify LESSON=NN REF=explore-it/lesson-MM` builds historical
binaries in a temporary independent Compose stack and runs current reproduction
scripts against them. `make dwell LESSON=NN` reports those probes across tags.
Test output belongs in ignored results/. `make down` deletes this stack's volume.

### Observe jobs and control lab time

`qctl job events ID` returns retained namespace-scoped history, including after
job deletion; `qctl watch QUEUE` polls histories for up to 500 jobs once per real second. Rows identify the
queue, worker, attempt, event time, and notification outbox/status/error. New
attempts retain their lease start separately from completion. Pre-hook leases
have unknown (`null`) starts; no timing history is invented. `event_at` uses
application time. API lifecycle JSON logs mirror committed events asynchronously;

# Queuelet

A small durable job queue: Go HTTP API, PostgreSQL storage, workers, cron schedules
and a webhook outbox. The CLI and the HTTP API expose the same operations.

Requirements: Go 1.26, Docker with Compose, Python 3, curl. PostgreSQL tools are
available inside the database container; `jq` is useful for manual exploration.

```sh
make up
make seed
make verify LESSON=00
go run ./cmd/qctl queue ls
go run ./cmd/qctl enqueue imports --kind echo --payload '{"message":"hello"}'
go run ./cmd/qctl jobs ls imports
make logs
make down
```

The API listens at `http://localhost:18200`, the webhook sink at port 18201 and
PostgreSQL at port 15433. Seed keys are `acme-key`, `globex-key`, and `admin-key`.
Set `QUEUELET_URL` and `QUEUELET_KEY` to select a service and namespace.
`make seed` / `make reset` discard this stack's data and restore 300 mixed-state
jobs, queues emails/reports/imports, two schedules and two running workers.
`results/manifest.json` contains the fixture ids and keys. Workers consume emails
and reports; imports is available for manual work. The local fixture credentials
are not intended for deployment.

```sh
go run ./cmd/qctl worker create manual --kinds echo
go run ./cmd/qctl lease imports --worker-id 4 --max-jobs 1
go run ./cmd/qctl job ack 123 --lease-token TOKEN --result '{"done":true}'
go run ./cmd/qctl job get 123
go run ./cmd/qctl job attempts 123
go run ./cmd/qctl stats imports
```

Use the returned worker/job ids and lease token in those examples. Worker mode:
`go run ./cmd/qctl worker run imports --kinds echo,sleep,fail,fail3,crash,http`.
Echo returns its payload; sleep reads payload.seconds; fail reads payload.n (or
use kind fail3); crash exits the worker; http GETs payload.url with a timeout.

Queue verbs: create, ls, get, patch, pause, resume, purge, rm.
Job verbs: get, attempts, ack, nack, heartbeat, cancel, retry, rm.
`batch <queue> --json '{"jobs":[…]}'` enqueues a batch.
`schedule create --json '{"name":"hourly","queue":"imports","kind":"echo","payload":{},"cron":"0 * * * *","timezone":"UTC"}'`
creates a schedule; schedule ls/get/patch/run/rm manage it.
Commands accepting arbitrary configuration use `--json`. A raw HTTP request is
also useful when exploring request structure:

```sh
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer acme-key' http://localhost:18200/v1/queues
PGPASSWORD=explorer psql -h localhost -p 15433 -U explorer -d queuelet
curl -s http://localhost:18201/admin/records
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"mode":"500"}' http://localhost:18201/admin/mode
```

The read-only explorer role can inspect every table. Hooksink modes are ok, 500,
slow and timeout. DELETE /admin/records clears its delivery log.

Read [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) for intended behavior. Source starts in cmd/api and
internal/api; jobs owns lease transitions, schedule owns cron firing, webhook owns
outbox delivery, stats owns aggregate reads, and store wraps database access.
The schema is in migrations. The API applies migrations when starting.

`make test` runs unit tests; `make checks` runs integration checks against the
running service. `make verify LESSON=NN REF=explore-it/lesson-MM` builds historical
binaries in a temporary independent Compose stack and runs current reproduction
scripts against them. `make dwell LESSON=NN` reports those probes across tags.
Test output belongs in ignored results/. `make down` deletes this stack's volume.

### Observe jobs and control lab time

`qctl job events ID` returns retained namespace-scoped history, including after
job deletion; `qctl watch QUEUE` polls histories for up to 500 jobs once per real second. Rows identify the
queue, worker, attempt, event time, and notification outbox/status/error. New
attempts retain their lease start separately from completion. Pre-hook leases
have unknown (`null`) starts; no timing history is invented. `event_at` uses
application time. API lifecycle JSON logs mirror committed events asynchronously;

# Experiment 03 — vary-it: notes

Explorer: fresh headless agent (Claude Opus 5.5), blind export `/tmp/explore-it-experiment-03` of `explore-it/lesson-02`.
Stack: own Compose project `queuelet-e03` (image tag e03; API 18240, hook 18241, PG 15473). Helper:
[tools/e03env.sh](tools/e03env.sh) (adapted copy of E02's `e02env.sh`; inherited copy unchanged). Raw outputs:
`project/results/e03/`. All timestamps UTC. `api M PATH ...` = raw curl as acme-key, prints body then `[HTTP status]`.

## 2026-10-22T04:12:00Z — start; reading

#read STATE.md, charter, PROTOCOL.md, skills/sweep-variables/SKILL.md, SPEC.md, defects INDEX, lesson 02,
models/variables.md, hypotheses.md.

Prior record relevant to this charter (all reported fixed in lesson 01): D05/D07/U06 range + charset (F19),
D06/U05 batch bounds + atomicity (F16), D08 payload precision (F17), D26/U07 unknown fields/enums (F20).
Passing re-checks of those are regressions, not discoveries.

## 2026-10-22T04:15Z — #read validators and serialization paths (lesson-02 source)

- `internal/api/api.go:49-58` `decode`: `json.NewDecoder` + `DisallowUnknownFields` + `UseNumber`, 2 MiB
  `MaxBytesReader`, **one** `Decode` call. Interpretation: trailing bytes after the first JSON value are never
  read, so `{...}garbage` or two concatenated objects should be accepted. Go `encoding/json` v1 matches field
  names case-insensitively, so `"KIND"` / `"Priority"` would not count as unknown. Content-Type not checked.
- `internal/api/enqueue.go:11-19` `JobInput`; `:26-73` `insertJob`: kind non-empty; run_at XOR delay; priority
  0–9; max_attempts ≥1 (no upper bound; DB `int` column); `delay_seconds` → `now.Add(time.Duration(d)*time.Second)`
  with no range check — int64 nanosecond overflow above 9 223 372 036 s; negative delay unchecked; payload must
  start with `{` and be `json.Valid`, stored as text into `jsonb` (migrations/001.sql:4).
- `enqueue.go:76-86`: any `insertJob` error (including DB errors) → 400 `invalid_job` with raw error text.
- `enqueue.go:88-120` batch: 1–500 elements, one transaction, any element error → 400 + rollback.
- `internal/api/queues.go:12-26` `QueueInput` includes `backoff.max_seconds` (`*int`) — **not in SPEC**.
  `:38` validation: name regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (no length bound), lease ≥1, max ≥1, retention ≥0 (float64,
  no upper bound), base ≥0 (no upper bound), kind linear|exponential; no check on max_seconds.
  `:46-49` any INSERT error → **409 queue_conflict** (also for numeric out-of-range on `int` columns).
- `queues.go:63-95` PATCH: lease/max/retention pointers with lower bounds; `webhook` is a struct pointer, and when
  present **both** url and secret are replaced (`:90-91`) — an omitted member becomes "". `:93-94` any UPDATE
  error → 500 via `output`.
- `grep backoff_max|MaxSeconds|max_seconds`: only queues.go:20, :46 and migrations/001.sql:3 — stored, never read.
- `internal/jobs/jobs.go:17-22` `Backoff`: linear `Duration(base*attempt)*Second`; exponential
  `Duration(base)*Second*Duration(1<<(attempt-1))` — unchecked int64 overflow; `internal/jobs/nack.go:22-26` uses
  it as `run_at = now + wait`.
- `internal/jobs/expire.go` `Retain`: SQL `finished_at < $1 - q.retention_hours * interval '1 hour'` for all
  queues in one statement; `internal/api/api.go:148-154` any step error sets coreFailed (health 503) and is
  logged; loop continues. Postgres timestamptz minimum is 4713 BC, so a large retention_hours could make the
  expression error for every tick.

## Variable inventory (before values) — charter surface: enqueue, batch, queue config

| Family | Variable | Heuristics to apply |
|---|---|---|
| request shape | trailing data, concatenated objects, duplicate keys, key case, Content-Type, empty body, `null` body, array body | Strings, Selection |
| enqueue fields | kind (empty, whitespace, long, NUL, case), payload (absent, null, array, nested, NUL escape, huge numbers, -0, 1E2, duplicate keys), priority (−1,0,9,10, 5.0, "5"), delay_seconds (−1, 0, huge, overflow), run_at (past, far future, no zone), max_attempts (0,1,int4 max, int4+1), idempotency_key ("" , repeat) | Boundaries, Numbers, Zero/One/Many, Goldilocks |
| batch | count (0,1,500,501), position of invalid element (first/middle/last), body size vs 2 MiB, duplicate idem keys | Count, Position, Beginning/Middle/End |
| queue create | name (charset, length 1 / huge), lease_seconds (0,1,int4 max, int4+1), max_attempts, retention_hours (0, fractional, huge), backoff.kind/base/max_seconds | Boundaries, Goldilocks, Some/None/All |
| queue patch | partial webhook object (url only / secret only), null members, out-of-range numbers | Some/None/All, Selection |
| timing/config interaction | backoff base × attempt number (overflow), retention × clock | Numbers, Boundaries |

## 2026-10-22T04:20Z — #hypothesis (all stated before any probe)

Charter prediction (H-C): "every documented range is enforced and unknown fields are rejected." Source: charter,
validators in internal/api. Wrong if any 2xx occurs where SPEC says 4xx. My own code-reading expectation is that
H-C will be refuted (E03-H01, -H02).

| Id | Prediction (code route) | Oracle (should) | Would be wrong if |

#read STATE.md, charter, PROTOCOL.md, skills/sweep-variables/SKILL.md, SPEC.md, defects INDEX, lesson 02,
models/variables.md, hypotheses.md.

Prior record relevant to this charter (all reported fixed in lesson 01): D05/D07/U06 range + charset (F19),

Passing re-checks of those are regressions, not discoveries.

## 2026-10-22T04:15Z — #read validators and serialization paths (lesson-02 source)

- `internal/api/api.go:49-58` `decode`: `json.NewDecoder` + `DisallowUnknownFields` + `UseNumber`, 2 MiB
  `MaxBytesReader`, **one** `Decode` call. Interpretation: trailing bytes after the first JSON value are never
  read, so `{...}garbage` or two concatenated objects should be accepted. Go `encoding/json` v1 matches field
  names case-insensitively, so `"KIND"` / `"Priority"` would not count as unknown. Content-Type not checked.
- `internal/api/enqueue.go:11-19` `JobInput`; `:26-73` `insertJob`: kind non-empty; run_at XOR delay; priority
  0–9; max_attempts ≥1 (no upper bound; DB `int` column); `delay_seconds` → `now.Add(time.Duration(d)*time.Second)`
  with no range check — int64 nanosecond overflow above 9 223 372 036 s; negative delay unchecked; payload must
  start with `{` and be `json.Valid`, stored as text into `jsonb` (migrations/001.sql:4).
- `enqueue.go:76-86`: any `insertJob` error (including DB errors) → 400 `invalid_job` with raw error text.
- `enqueue.go:88-120` batch: 1–500 elements, one transaction, any element error → 400 + rollback.
- `internal/api/queues.go:12-26` `QueueInput` includes `backoff.max_seconds` (`*int`) — **not in SPEC**.
  `:38` validation: name regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (no length bound), lease ≥1, max ≥1, retention ≥0 (float64,
  no upper bound), base ≥0 (no upper bound), kind linear|exponential; no check on max_seconds.
  `:46-49` any INSERT error → **409 queue_conflict** (also for numeric out-of-range on `int` columns).
- `queues.go:63-95` PATCH: lease/max/retention pointers with lower bounds; `webhook` is a struct pointer, and when
  present **both** url and secret are replaced (`:90-91`) — an omitted member becomes "". `:93-94` any UPDATE
  error → 500 via `output`.
- `grep backoff_max|MaxSeconds|max_seconds`: only queues.go:20, :46 and migrations/001.sql:3 — stored, never read.
- `internal/jobs/jobs.go:17-22` `Backoff`: linear `Duration(base*attempt)*Second`; exponential
  `Duration(base)*Second*Duration(1<<(attempt-1))` — unchecked int64 overflow; `internal/jobs/nack.go:22-26` uses
  it as `run_at = now + wait`.
- `internal/jobs/expire.go` `Retain`: SQL `finished_at < $1 - q.retention_hours * interval '1 hour'` for all
  queues in one statement; `internal/api/api.go:148-154` any step error sets coreFailed (health 503) and is
  logged; loop continues. Postgres timestamptz minimum is 4713 BC, so a large retention_hours could make the
  expression error for every tick.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""E03 helper: create a queue with a long name, then GET and DELETE it by that name.
Usage: namelen.py <kind:rep|rand> <length>. Uses QUEUELET_URL and acme-key."""
import json, os, random, string, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
base = os.environ["QUEUELET_URL"]
kind, n = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
random.seed(n)
name = "q" * n if kind == "rep" else "".join(random.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(n))
def call(method, path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 {"Authorization": "Bearer acme-key", "Content-Type": "application/json"}, method=method)
    try:

# E02-F02 — One unparsable webhook URL stops notification delivery for every queue and namespace

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-01` plain export; stack `queuelet-e02`, image `queuelet:e02`; fixture `lab/reset.sh` 03:23:12Z
  (blocking run) and 03:30:14Z (variable isolation).
- Original observation: [E02 notes](../experiments/02-make-it-visible/notes.md) E02-H11 (stated 03:28Z; observed 03:28:39Z–03:29:58Z),
  E02-H11a–d. Source of the prediction: E01 backlog H44 + `internal/webhook/ship.go:26-28`.

## Minimal reproduction
1. Any namespace (here globex-key): `POST /v1/queues {"name":"e02bad","webhook":{"url":"http://bad host/x","secret":"s"}}` → 201.
2. Create a worker, enqueue an echo job, lease it, ack it (job 305) → 200; outbox row 71 is created with that URL.
3. In another namespace (acme), complete a job on a webhook queue: `POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs {"kind":"echo",…}` → 306,
   acked by worker-b.
4. Watch `webhook_outbox`, hooksink `/admin/records`, `/health`, api log for 20 s.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:121 "Failed notifications are retried. Delivery is at least once." SPEC:10 "A namespace key accesses only its
namespace's resources" (tenant isolation, approximation: one tenant's configuration must not deny service to another).
SPEC:17 commands with invalid values "should be rejected as invalid commands" (a URL that can never be requested).

## Observed
```text
create/PATCH with "http://bad host/x" → 201 / 200 (no validation, queues.go:21-41, :79-84)
outbox 71 (job 305, globex) attempts 0 undelivered; outbox 72 (job 306, acme) attempts 0 undelivered for 24 s (20/20 samples)
hooksink records: 0
/health: 503 {"status":"degraded"} (cause not stated)
api log, every second: webhook task: parse "http://bad host/x": invalid character " " in host name
```
`Ship` selects due rows `ORDER BY id LIMIT 20` and `return e` on `http.NewRequest` error before updating attempts/next_at
(`ship.go:17-28`), so the same row is first on every tick and nothing after it is attempted.

## Variables isolated
- Recovery via the API does not exist: PATCH the queue to a valid URL → still blocked (outbox copies the URL at Notify,
  `jobs.go:80`); DELETE the job (204) → orphan outbox row 71 remains and still blocks (H11a/b, 03:29:42–03:29:58Z).
- Failure class matters: `ftp://x/y` (parses, fails in `Do`) is a per-row failure, attempts+1 every 5 s, does **not** block
  (H11c, 03:30:46–03:30:59Z). Only NewRequest-time errors block.
- Namespace does not matter (cross-tenant shown). Hooksink mode irrelevant (ok throughout).
- Lab reset (TRUNCATE) cleared it; no restart was tried (row persists in DB, so restart is predicted not to help — not probed).

## Sibling check
- `queues.go:79-84` PATCH accepts the same URL (observed 200, H11d) — same entry point to the blocking state.
- Other `return e` inside the Ship row loop: the two `UPDATE webhook_outbox` errors (`ship.go:37-40`, `:46-49`) — DB errors,
  would also abort the batch (not probed). `secret` type assertion `r["secret"].(string)` (`ship.go:23`) would panic on NULL;
  Notify always writes text (inference).
- Outbox rows survive job deletion (no FK, migrations/001.sql:10) — orphan source (C10 sibling).

## Severity / status
High: any tenant can, by mistake or on purpose, silently stop all webhook notifications for all tenants until an operator
edits the database; health shows only "degraded". Status: open.

# E03-F01 — Malformed JSON request bodies are accepted: trailing data ignored, a second object silently dropped, invalid UTF-8 rewritten

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`, image `queuelet:e03`; fixture `lab/seed/seed.py` 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H01 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:16:44Z),
  E03-H16 (04:17:32Z), batch sibling (04:23:09Z), PATCH sibling E03-H19 (04:24:21Z). Raw: `project/results/e03/p1-shape.txt`,
  `p3-numbers.txt`, `p9b-payload-batch.txt`, `p10-siblings.txt`. Prediction source: `internal/api/api.go:49-58`.

## Minimal reproduction
Any namespace key, any existing queue (here acme `imports`, which has no Compose worker):
1. `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer acme-key' $QUEUELET_URL/v1/queues/imports/jobs -d '{"kind":"echo","payload":{"t":"h01a"}} trailing-garbage'`
2. `... -d '{"kind":"echo","payload":{"t":"h01b"}}{"kind":"second","payload":{"t":"h01b2"}}'`
3. `printf '{"kind":"ech\xffo","payload":{"t":"h16-utf8"}}' > f.json; curl ... --data-binary @f.json`
4. Read back the rows (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` or read-only SQL).

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:15-17 — commands are JSON; "Unknown fields and invalid enum values should be rejected as invalid commands" (the
service should reject what it does not understand). RFC 8259 §2: a JSON text is exactly one value surrounded by optional
whitespace, so `{…} trailing-garbage` and `{…}{…}` are not JSON texts; RFC 8259 §8.1: JSON exchanged between systems MUST
be UTF-8. Expected 400 `invalid_json` and nothing stored.

## Observed
```text
1 → {"id":301,"state":"queued"} [201]   stored {"t": "h01a"}
2 → {"id":302,"state":"queued"} [201]   stored kind echo {"t": "h01b"}; no job of kind "second" exists
3 → {"id":831,"state":"queued"} [201]   stored kind "ech�o" (hex 656368efbfbd6f — U+FFFD substituted)
control: '{"kind":"echo",}' → 400 invalid_json (a malformed *first* value is rejected)
```
Cause (code route, consistent with the observations): `decode` calls `json.Decoder.Decode` once and never checks for
EOF afterwards (`api.go:50-53`); Go's decoder converts invalid UTF-8 inside strings to U+FFFD.

## Variables isolated
- Trailing content: arbitrary text and a complete second JSON object both ignored; the second object's command is lost
  with a 201 for the request as a whole.
- Endpoint: job enqueue (H01), queue create (`{"name":"e03-trail"}{"name":"other"}` → 201, no `other` queue), batch
  (`{"jobs":[…]} {"jobs":[]}` → 201 one id), queue PATCH (`{"MAX_ATTEMPTS":5} garbage` → 200 applied).
- Invalid UTF-8 placement: inside a `string` field (kind) → silently rewritten; inside the raw `payload` → rejected 400 by
  PostgreSQL (`pq: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0xff`), so the payload path is not affected.
- Did not matter: Content-Type (text/plain also accepted, see notes Q-E03-1), namespace.

## Sibling check
Every handler that uses `decode` (`internal/api/api.go:49`): queue create/PATCH (`queues.go:35`, `:77`; observed), enqueue and
batch (`enqueue.go:78`, `:92`; observed), ack/nack/heartbeat (`jobs.go:60`; not probed with trailing data), worker create,
lease, schedules create/PATCH, `/admin/clock` (`observe.go:25`) — predicted identical by code, not probed.
Case-insensitive member matching is a separate decoder leniency: [E03-F02](E03-F02-case-variant-member-names-accepted.md).

## Severity / status
Low–medium: a client or proxy that concatenates or mis-frames requests gets a 2xx while part of its command is discarded;
corrupted kind strings are stored as if valid. Status: open.

# E03-F02 — Case-variant member names (`KIND`, `Priority`, `LEASE_TOKEN`) are accepted as the documented fields; the last variant wins

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H02 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:16:44Z); siblings
  batch (04:23:09Z), E03-H19/H20 (04:24:21Z, rerun 04:24:37Z). Raw: `project/results/e03/p1-shape.txt`, `p9b-payload-batch.txt`,
  `p10-siblings.txt`, `p10b-siblings.txt`. Prediction source: `internal/api/api.go:49-52` (Go `encoding/json` v1 field matching).

## Minimal reproduction
1. `POST /v1/queues/imports/jobs -d '{"KIND":"echo","Priority":3,"PAYLOAD":{"t":"h02a"}}'` (acme-key).
2. `POST /v1/queues/imports/jobs -d '{"kind":"echo","priority":1,"PRIORITY":9,"payload":{"t":"h02b"}}'`.
3. `POST /v1/queues/imports/jobs -d '{"kind":"echo","PRIORITY":9,"priority":1,"payload":{"t":"h02c"}}'`.
4. Read the stored kind/priority.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:17 "Unknown fields … should be rejected as invalid commands." JSON member names are strings and are compared exactly
(RFC 8259 §8.3); `KIND` is not the documented `kind`. Expected 400 `invalid_json` "unknown field".

## Observed
```text
1 → 201 id 303: kind echo, priority 3, payload {"t": "h02a"}
2 → 201 id 304: priority 9   (later case-variant overrides the exact name)
3 → 201 id 305: priority 1
queue create {"NAME":"e03-case","Lease_Seconds":7} → 201, lease_seconds 7
batch {"JOBS":[{"Kind":"echo",…}]} → 201 {"ids":[1363]}
PATCH {"MAX_ATTEMPTS":5} → 200 max_attempts 5
ack {"LEASE_TOKEN":"<token>","RESULT":{"ok":1}} → 200; job 1369 succeeded, result {"ok": 1}
control: {"kind":"echo","x":1} → 400 `json: unknown field "x"` (exact unknown names are rejected)
```

## Variables isolated
- Key order: whichever spelling appears last wins (2 vs 3), so an exact-name value can be overridden by a variant later in the body.
- Applies to top-level and nested members (`PAYLOAD`, `JOBS[].Kind`) and to worker-protocol fields (`LEASE_TOKEN`).
- Exact duplicate keys (`"kind":"echo","kind":"other"` → kind other) behave the same way but RFC 8259 leaves duplicate-name
  behaviour implementation-defined, so that part alone is not claimed as a defect.

## Sibling check
All `decode` users (`internal/api/api.go:49`, list in [E03-F01](E03-F01-malformed-json-text-accepted.md)); the worker/qctl clients
send exact names so they are unaffected. `DisallowUnknownFields` (`api.go:51`) is the lesson-01 fix for D26; this is a gap in
that fix rather than a regression of it.

## Severity / status
Low–medium: a gateway or validator that inspects `priority`/`lease_token` case-sensitively can be bypassed by a variant
spelling that queuelet honours (parameter smuggling); clients with typos in casing get silent success. Status: open.

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; real clock; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H04 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:17:32Z); siblings
  E03-H17, E03-H18 (stated 04:24Z, observed 04:24:21Z). Raw: `project/results/e03/p3-numbers.txt`, `p10-siblings.txt`.
  Prediction source: `internal/api/enqueue.go:57-58` (`time.Duration(*in.DelaySeconds) * time.Second`, no range check).

## Minimal reproduction
1. `POST /v1/queues/imports/jobs -d '{"kind":"echo","delay_seconds":9223372037,"payload":{}}'` (acme-key).
2. Compare with `delay_seconds: 9223372036`.
3. Read `state`/`run_at`.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:46-47 "Choose either delay in seconds … A job due now is `queued`; a future job is `scheduled`." A delay of
9 223 372 037 s is in the future; the service must either schedule it at now + delay or reject a delay it cannot represent
(SPEC:17 invalid command → 400). It must never run it now.

## Observed
```text
delay 9223372036          → 201 scheduled, run_at 2319-02-01 04:04:49 (honoured)
delay 9223372037          → 201 queued,    run_at 1734-07-13 04:30:16 (wrapped ≈292 y into the past)
delay 100000000000        → 201 scheduled, run_at 2272-11-28 16:11:24 (asked ≈3169 y; a different, wrapped future)
delay 9223372036854775807 → 201 queued,    run_at now − 1 s
delay 9223372036854775808 → 400 invalid_json (does not fit Go int)
```

## Variables isolated
- Boundary is exactly the Go `time.Duration` range (2^63 − 1 ns ≈ 9 223 372 036.85 s); 9 223 372 036 is honoured, +1 wraps.
- Outcome above the boundary depends on the value modulo 2^64 ns: past (runs now) or an arbitrary wrong future.
- Not affected: `run_at` (parsed as an absolute time; 9999-12-31 → scheduled correctly); negative delay (queued; SPEC silent, not claimed).

## Sibling check (predicted before probing, then observed)
- `internal/jobs/nack.go:23-24` nack `delay_seconds` override: 9223372037 → 200, `retry_wait` run_at 1734-07-13, queued 1.5 s
  later (E03-H17, job 1365) — a "retry much later" request becomes an immediate retry.
- `internal/jobs/jobs.go:84` heartbeat `extend_seconds`: 9223372037 → 200 `{"ok":true}`, lease_expires_at 1734-07-13; 1.5 s
  later the job was `queued`, attempts 1, last_error "lease expired" (E03-H18, job 1366) — asking for a longer lease ends it
  and consumes an attempt.
- `internal/jobs/jobs.go:17-22` queue backoff — same arithmetic family, separate report [E03-F06](E03-F06-backoff-overflow-immediate-retry.md).
- `jobs.go:61,65` lease expiry `Duration(sec)*Second`: `lease_seconds` is an `int` column (≤ 2 147 483 647), so it cannot
  overflow (inference; 2147483647 was accepted, expiry not observed).
- `internal/clock/clock.go:40-42` explicitly range-checks its `advance` — the one place that guards this arithmetic.

## Severity / status
Medium: a caller's explicit "not before" intent is inverted — work runs ~immediately and a heartbeat can kill its own lease.
Inputs are unusual but accepted with 2xx and no indication. Status: open.

SPEC:12-16: errors are 4xx/5xx JSON; "A command incompatible with the current state returns 409." An out-of-range number or a
name the store cannot index is an invalid command, not a state conflict and not a server fault → 400 with a service-level
message. (Approximation: RFC 9110 §15.5.10 defines 409 as a conflict with the target resource's current state.)

## Observed

1 → 409 {"error":{"code":"queue_conflict","message":"pq: value \"2147483648\" is out of range for type integer"}}

2 → 500 {"error":{"code":"database_error","message":"pq: value \"2147483648\" is out of range for type integer"}} (also max_attempts)
3 → 409 {"error":{"code":"queue_conflict","message":"pq: index row size 2824 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index \"qu…"}}
    random 10 000 chars → 409 "pq: index row requires 10024 bytes, maximum size is 8191"; random 2 600 → 201 (GET 200, DELETE 204)
    "q"×100 000 → 201 (GET 200, DELETE 204); "q"×900 000 / ×1 100 000 → 409 "index row requires …"
control: duplicate name → 409 queue_conflict (the one legitimate conflict uses the same code)
```

- Field: every `int`-backed queue field fails the same way above 2^31 − 1; per-job `max_attempts` 2147483648 on enqueue is a
  correct 400 `invalid_job` (still driver text) because enqueue maps all insert errors to 400.

- Name length: the effective limit is undocumented and depends on compressibility of the name (≈2 700 bytes random, ≥100 000
  repetitive) because it is the btree index-row limit after TOAST compression.
- A client cannot distinguish "name taken" from "value too large" by status or code.

- `internal/api/queues.go:93-94` PATCH `output()` → 500 for any DB error (observed).
- `internal/api/api.go:173-179` `output` is shared by list/stats/attempts reads — DB errors there are true 500s (fine).
- `internal/api/enqueue.go:85-87` maps every insert error (including real DB outages) to 400 `invalid_job` — the opposite
  misclassification for a DB fault (inference, not probed).
- Schedules create (`schedules.go`) — not probed (#offcharter).
- Driver text in messages: E01 Q3 (open question) — same leak.

## Severity / status
Low: no data corruption; clients and operators get a misleading error class (409 suggests retry-after-rename; 500 suggests a
server incident) and internal driver text. Status: open.

# E03-F05 — One queue's large `retention_hours` stops terminal-job retention for every queue in every namespace and holds /health at 503

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; real clock; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H09 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:18:27Z–04:19:23Z).
  Raw: `project/results/e03/p4-queuecfg.txt`, `p5-retention.txt`, `p5b-retention-isolate.txt`, `all-logs-at-stop.txt`.
  Prediction source: `internal/jobs/expire.go` `Retain` (one statement over all queues:
  `finished_at < $1 - q.retention_hours * interval '1 hour'`), `internal/api/queues.go:38` (retention only `>= 0`),
  `internal/api/api.go:148-154`.

## Minimal reproduction
1. acme: `POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"e03-ret-1e8","retention_hours":1e8}'` → 201. (`1e308` also works; see below.)
2. Enqueue one job there and cancel it (`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` → 200), so the queue owns a terminal job.
3. Any namespace: a queue with `retention_hours: 0`; enqueue + cancel a job (control that should be removed on the next tick).
4. Poll the control row, `GET /health`, and the API log for ≥5 s.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:85 "Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`" (for each queue, by its own setting); SPEC:24 retention hours must
be nonnegative — 1e8 is a valid nonnegative value, so it must either work (keep that queue's jobs ~11 400 years) or be
rejected with 400 at create/PATCH (SPEC:17). SPEC:10 approximation: one namespace's configuration must not deny service to
another. SPEC:117-120: health reports real loop degradation.

## Observed
```text
before poison: control job 832 (retention 0) cancelled 04:18:27.686 → removed by 04:18:28.404 (event "retained" 04:18:28.010)
poison job 833 cancelled 04:18:28.582; control job 834 cancelled immediately after
04:18:29.700 … 04:18:35.224 (6 samples): /health {"status":"degraded"} [503]; job 834 still present
api log each second: {"msg":"background task: pq: timestamp out of range"}
globex queue gx-ret0 (retention 0): job 836 cancelled 04:18:57 → still present 04:19:01.859
Promote unaffected: delayed job 835 promoted to queued within 3 s
PATCH e03-ret-1e8 retention 24 → 04:19:04.580 health ok; acme 834 and globex 836 removed on that tick
```

## Variables isolated
- Entry point: create and PATCH (`PATCH {"retention_hours":1e8}` → 200 → degraded again 04:19:06.893).
- Magnitude: 5e7 h + terminal job → ok; 6e7 h → degraded (bracket observed). This matches the timestamp minimum (4713 BC
  ≈ 6 739 years ≈ 5.9e7 h before 2026; reason inferred). `1e308` fails differently: log "pq: interval out of range" → degraded.
- Trigger requires a terminal job in the poisoned queue: the queues sat harmless while empty (04:17:59–04:18:28).
- Namespace: globex retention blocked by an acme setting. Promotion, expiry and webhook shipping continued (Promote observed;
  others inferred from loop order `api.go:148`).
- Recovery: lowering retention (04:19:04) or deleting the terminal job (`DELETE /v1/jobs/833` → 204 → ok 04:19:08.947).

## Sibling check
- `queues.go:80` PATCH accepts the same values (observed).
- Other SQL interval arithmetic on stored config: none found in `internal/` besides Retain (grep `interval`); expiry/backoff are
  computed in Go (`jobs.go:61`, `nack.go:22-26`, see [E03-F06](E03-F06-backoff-overflow-immediate-retry.md)).
- Schedules (`schedule/fire.go`) evaluate per row in Go — not probed (#offcharter).

## Severity / status
High: a single accepted configuration value in any tenant silently disables retention for all tenants (unbounded table growth,
SPEC:85 violated everywhere) and pins health at 503 with no cause named, until someone finds and edits that queue or job.
Status: open.

# E03-F07 — Undocumented `backoff.max_seconds` is accepted, stored and echoed (even negative) but never applied

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; real clock; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H07 (stated 04:16Z; acceptance observed 04:17:59Z,
  effect 04:19:56Z and 04:20:13Z). Raw: `project/results/e03/p4-queuecfg.txt`, `p6-backoff.txt`, `p6b-backoff-controls.txt`.
  Prediction source: `internal/api/queues.go:20,46`; grep of `backoff_max|MaxSeconds|max_seconds` finds no reader.

## Minimal reproduction
1. `POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"e03-maxs2","backoff":{"kind":"exponential","base_seconds":10,"max_seconds":1}}'` → 201,
   response `"backoff_max":1`.
2. Register an echo worker, enqueue, lease, `nack {"lease_token":…,"error":"x"}` (no delay override).
3. Read `run_at`.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:17 unknown fields should be rejected; SPEC:24-27 documents the backoff object as `kind` and `base_seconds` only — so
`max_seconds` is an unknown field → 400. If it is instead a supported field, a cap of 1 s must bound the retry wait, and a
negative cap must be rejected (SPEC:25-26 nonnegative seconds).

## Observed
```text
create e03-maxs  {base 4,  max_seconds -7} → 201 "backoff_max":-7
create e03-maxs2 {base 10, max_seconds 1}  → 201 "backoff_max":1
e03-maxs  job 842 nack at 04:19:56.169 → run_at 04:20:00.190 (+4 s  = base·2^0; cap ignored)
e03-maxs2 job 844 nack at 04:20:13.643 → run_at 04:20:23.621 (+10 s = base·2^0; cap of 1 s ignored)
max_seconds 2147483648 → 409 queue_conflict (int column; E03-F04)
```

## Variables isolated
- Positive and negative caps both have no effect; validation runs on none of them.
- Not PATCHable (`PATCH {"backoff":…}` → 400 unknown field), so the stored value cannot be corrected either.

## Sibling check
- Other accepted-but-unread inputs in the queue/job inputs: none found — every other `QueueInput`/`JobInput` field is used in
  the INSERT and read by lease/nack/expire/retain (`jobs.go`, `nack.go`, `expire.go`).
- Interaction: an honoured cap would also have bounded the overflow in [E03-F06](E03-F06-backoff-overflow-immediate-retry.md).

## Severity / status
Low–medium: operators who set a cap believe retries are bounded (e.g. "never wait more than 60 s") while exponential waits grow
without limit; the API confirms the setting back to them. Status: open (spec decision: reject the field or implement it).

# E03-F08 — PATCH with a partial `webhook` object clears the omitted member: secret-only disables notifications, URL-only drops the signing secret

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; hooksink mode ok; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H10 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:21:40Z–04:22:03Z).
  Raw: `project/results/e03/p7-patch-webhook.txt`, `p8-misc.txt`. Prediction source: `internal/api/queues.go:72-75, 85-92`.

## Minimal reproduction
1. `POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"e03-hook","webhook":{"url":"http://hooksink:8201/hook","secret":"report-secret"}}'`.
2. `PATCH /v1/queues/e03-hook -d '{"webhook":{"secret":"rotated"}}'`; enqueue and cancel a job; inspect `webhook_outbox`.
3. Restore, then `PATCH … -d '{"webhook":{"url":"http://hooksink:8201/hook"}}'`; cancel a job; read hooksink `/admin/records`.

## Expected (oracle)
Approximation, because SPEC does not define merge depth: SPEC:30-31 "PATCH … updates … webhook settings", and the same
endpoint treats an omitted top-level member as "keep" (observed: `{"max_attempts":4}` keeps the webhook). RFC 7396 (JSON
Merge Patch) applies the same rule recursively: omitted members are unchanged. SPEC (notification destinations section) says
only an *empty URL* disables future notifications — not an omitted one. Expected: secret-only PATCH keeps the URL;
URL-only PATCH keeps the secret.

## Observed
```text
PATCH {"webhook":{"secret":"rotated"}}  → 200 "webhook_secret":"rotated","webhook_url":""
  job 847 cancelled → 0 outbox rows (notification silently not produced)
  control: url+secret restored, job 848 cancelled → outbox row delivered
PATCH {"webhook":{"url":"…/hook2"}}     → 200 "webhook_secret":"","webhook_url":"…/hook2"
  (url-only on …/hook) job 849 cancelled → hooksink record status 200, "signature_valid":false; outbox secret '' delivered t
PATCH {"webhook":{}} → both cleared;  PATCH {"webhook":null} → both unchanged
```

## Variables isolated
- Only the nested object is replaced wholesale; top-level members merge (COALESCE, `queues.go:93`).
- `null` vs `{}` differ: null keeps, empty object clears both.
- Partner view: queuelet records the unsigned notification as delivered (2xx), so neither side surfaces the lost secret.

## Sibling check
- Schedule PATCH (`internal/api/schedules.go`) uses pointer fields for cron/timezone/enabled (no nested object) — not probed
  (#offcharter). Queue create has no merge question. No other nested objects in PATCH bodies found.

## Severity / status
Medium: a routine secret rotation silently turns off all notifications for the queue, and a URL migration silently stops
signing them; both return 200 with the changed values echoed only in the response body. Status: open (needs a spec line on
nested merge semantics).

Approximation, because SPEC does not define merge depth: SPEC:30-31 "PATCH … updates … webhook settings", and the same
endpoint treats an omitted top-level member as "keep" (observed: `{"max_attempts":4}` keeps the webhook). RFC 7396 (JSON
Merge Patch) applies the same rule recursively: omitted members are unchanged. SPEC (notification destinations section) says
only an *empty URL* disables future notifications — not an omitted one. Expected: secret-only PATCH keeps the URL;
URL-only PATCH keeps the secret.

## Observed
```text
PATCH {"webhook":{"secret":"rotated"}}  → 200 "webhook_secret":"rotated","webhook_url":""
  job 847 cancelled → 0 outbox rows (notification silently not produced)
  control: url+secret restored, job 848 cancelled → outbox row delivered
PATCH {"webhook":{"url":"…/hook2"}}     → 200 "webhook_secret":"","webhook_url":"…/hook2"
  (url-only on …/hook) job 849 cancelled → hooksink record status 200, "signature_valid":false; outbox secret '' delivered t
PATCH {"webhook":{}} → both cleared;  PATCH {"webhook":null} → both unchanged
```

## Variables isolated
- Only the nested object is replaced wholesale; top-level members merge (COALESCE, `queues.go:93`).
- `null` vs `{}` differ: null keeps, empty object clears both.
- Partner view: queuelet records the unsigned notification as delivered (2xx), so neither side surfaces the lost secret.

## Sibling check
- Schedule PATCH (`internal/api/schedules.go`) uses pointer fields for cron/timezone/enabled (no nested object) — not probed
  (#offcharter). Queue create has no merge question. No other nested objects in PATCH bodies found.

## Severity / status
Medium: a routine secret rotation silently turns off all notifications for the queue, and a URL migration silently stops
signing them; both return 200 with the changed values echoed only in the response body. Status: open (needs a spec line on
nested merge semantics).

# E03-F05 — One queue's large `retention_hours` stops terminal-job retention for every queue in every namespace and holds /health at 503

- Seen at: `explore-it/lesson-02` plain export; stack `queuelet-e03`; real clock; fixture seed 04:16:24Z.
- Original observation: [E03 notes](../experiments/03-vary-it/notes.md) E03-H09 (stated 04:16Z, observed 04:18:27Z–04:19:23Z).
  Raw: `project/results/e03/p4-queuecfg.txt`, `p5-retention.txt`, `p5b-retention-isolate.txt`, `all-logs-at-stop.txt`.
  Prediction source: `internal/jobs/expire.go` `Retain` (one statement over all queues:
  `finished_at < $1 - q.retention_hours * interval '1 hour'`), `internal/api/queues.go:38` (retention only `>= 0`),
  `internal/api/api.go:148-154`.

## Minimal reproduction
1. acme: `POST /v1/queues -d '{"name":"e03-ret-1e8","retention_hours":1e8}'` → 201. (`1e308` also works; see below.)
2. Enqueue one job there and cancel it (`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` → 200), so the queue owns a terminal job.
3. Any namespace: a queue with `retention_hours: 0`; enqueue + cancel a job (control that should be removed on the next tick).
4. Poll the control row, `GET /health`, and the API log for ≥5 s.

## Expected (oracle)
SPEC:85 "Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`" (for each queue, by its own setting); SPEC:24 retention hours must
be nonnegative — 1e8 is a valid nonnegative value, so it must either work (keep that queue's jobs ~11 400 years) or be
rejected with 400 at create/PATCH (SPEC:17). SPEC:10 approximation: one namespace's configuration must not deny service to
another. SPEC:117-120: health reports real loop degradation.

## Observed
```text
before poison: control job 832 (retention 0) cancelled 04:18:27.686 → removed by 04:18:28.404 (event "retained" 04:18:28.010)
poison job 833 cancelled 04:18:28.582; control job 834 cancelled immediately after
04:18:29.700 … 04:18:35.224 (6 samples): /health {"status":"degraded"} [503]; job 834 still present
api log each second: {"msg":"background task: pq: timestamp out of range"}
globex queue gx-ret0 (retention 0): job 836 cancelled 04:18:57 → still present 04:19:01.859
Promote unaffected: delayed job 835 promoted to queued within 3 s
PATCH e03-ret-1e8 retention 24 → 04:19:04.580 health ok; acme 834 and globex 836 removed on that tick
```

## Variables isolated
- Entry point: create and PATCH (`PATCH {"retention_hours":1e8}` → 200 → degraded again 04:19:06.893).
- Magnitude: 5e7 h + terminal job → ok; 6e7 h → degraded (bracket observed). This matches the timestamp minimum (4713 BC
  ≈ 6 739 years ≈ 5.9e7 h before 2026; reason inferred). `1e308` fails differently: log "pq: interval out of range" → degraded.
- Trigger requires a terminal job in the poisoned queue: the queues sat harmless while empty (04:17:59–04:18:28).
- Namespace: globex retention blocked by an acme setting. Promotion, expiry and webhook shipping continued (Promote observed;
  others inferred from loop order `api.go:148`).
- Recovery: lowering retention (04:19:04) or deleting the terminal job (`DELETE /v1/jobs/833` → 204 → ok 04:19:08.947).

## Sibling check
- `queues.go:80` PATCH accepts the same values (observed).
- Other SQL interval arithmetic on stored config: none found in `internal/` besides Retain (grep `interval`); expiry/backoff are
  computed in Go (`jobs.go:61`, `nack.go:22-26`, see [E03-F06](E03-F06-backoff-overflow-immediate-retry.md)).
- Schedules (`schedule/fire.go`) evaluate per row in Go — not probed (#offcharter).

## Severity / status
High: a single accepted configuration value in any tenant silently disables retention for all tenants (unbounded table growth,
SPEC:85 violated everywhere) and pins health at 503 with no cause named, until someone finds and edits that queue or job.
Status: open.

10:A namespace key accesses only its namespace's resources.
12:JSON commands use `Content-Type: application/json`.
13:Errors have the form `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}` and a 4xx or 5xx
15:Creation returns 201. Deletion returns 204. A missing resource returns 404.
16:A command incompatible with the current state returns 409.
17:Unknown fields and invalid enum values should be rejected as invalid commands.
22:Names use ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.
23:Configuration defaults are `lease_seconds:30`, `max_attempts:3`,
25:Lease duration and maximum attempts must be positive; retention hours must be nonnegative.
26:Backoff kind is `linear` or `exponential`; the base is a nonnegative number
27:of seconds. Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff from `base_seconds`
28:or linear backoff when configured.
33:`PATCH /v1/queues/{name}` updates lease duration, maximum attempts, retention
34:or webhook settings. Existing jobs retain their maximum-attempt setting.
46:Kind is required. Priority ranges from 0 through 9 and defaults to 5.
47:Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric precision.
48:Choose either delay in seconds or an RFC3339 `run_at`, never both.
49:A job due now is `queued`; a future job is `scheduled`.
52:Repeated use of an idempotency key within a queue returns the original job.
54:`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs:batch` accepts `{"jobs":[…]}` with 1–500 jobs.
55:An empty or oversized batch is invalid and returns 400 without insertion.
56:A batch is atomic: an invalid element leaves none of its new jobs stored.

88:An expired lease records an unsuccessful attempt and releases the job for retry
98:Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
127:The background loop promotes scheduled jobs, expires leases, fires cron schedules,
129:lifecycle progress. Health reports database availability and loop degradation;
136:an empty URL disables future notification snapshots. Each completed job's outbox
